_comment: Settings of every map build, read by `workers/plan/options.py` – the run forms
ask only what to build, the rest is here and the run's first job prints it.
A value is looked up from the most specific place: a region in `maps.<country>.regions`,
then its country, then `defaults`; a range in `maps.mountains.ranges`, then
`maps.mountains`, then `defaults`. A range takes nothing from a country.
defaults        every key there is, with what it means in `options.py`
maps            countries as in `regions` and the category `mountains`
sources.aerial  aerial photo sources; a map picks one with `aerial_summer`/`aerial_winter`
credits         data authors; every source names its own in `credits`
sources.dem     height models; a map picks them with `*_source`
regions         every map's place: name, bbox, osm.fr extract, country
areas           named cut-outs (ranges) for the `area` input and the ranges
maps.mountains.ranges  a range's cut-out, countries and OSM extracts beside its settings
Tuning: change the value here on a branch and run the workflow from that branch.
Height models for three settings: `contour_source` (contours), `rock_source`
(rocks) and `shading_source` (shading and 3D terrain). The `for` key of each
source says for which of the three it may be picked – `workers/lint/settings.py`
keeps every level of the settings to it.
One source for everything (the old `dem_source` input) held while only one
was verified. With several models it stopped making sense: rocks want the
finest model available, shading can do with a coarser one but must cover the
whole region. Three choices say that, and nothing is quietly substituted.
THREE MODELS, EACH FOR A REASON:
sonny   20 m, verified, the default. Covers everything, never missing.
dmr35   10 m, ÚGKK open data. Twice as fine as Sonny and downloads as
one ZIP – still the cheapest improvement in detail.
dmr5    LiDAR. 1 m with a cutout, 5 m for a whole region. The best we
have, and for rocks the only one that really shows a crag's shape.
A FOURTH SOURCE `ugkk` IS GONE. It was the same model as `dmr5`, just its
1 m form for a cutout – two keys for one LiDAR. `dmr5` now picks its form by
extent itself (see its `_comment`), so it works fully in shading too – that
always covers a whole region and gets the 5 m version.
Rocks also have `tienovanie` – ready polygons from dark hillshade areas.
It isn't an elevation model, so it isn't in this list.
ÚGKK licence: free use including commercial, with the source credited
(ÚGKK SR). That must be in the map attribution – see poc/web/themes.js.

sonny1.label: Sonny's LiDAR DTM 1″ (.hgt)
_comment: Sonny's second model, from a Drive folder:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FCXPutDU6DvnTEA4PY6iFOQKiuVd11j4
WHAT THE FOLDER REALLY HOLDS (read 2026-08-11, not guessed):
15 tiles N47E017 … N49E022, each as `<tile>.zip`
one `<tile>.hgt` per ZIP, 25 934 402 B = 3601 × 3601 × int16
~146 MB to download in all (measured on 11 tiles, 7.0–11.6 MB)
plus `_Readme.txt` and `_Region.jpg` (a coverage map)
CRS       EPSG:4326, WGS 84; big-endian byte order
heights   above sea level in the national system (Bpv), NOT ellipsoidal
nodata    -32768; not a single point in N49E020 (Tatras)
The folder is called “…1asec v1”, but its `_Readme.txt` is VERSION 2
(2023-06-27, “Complete coverage with DTM v5.0”). The folder name says
nothing about the version – go by the readme.
ITS SOURCE IS DMR 5.0, resampled to 1″ and rounded to whole metres. In
Slovakia it's the same LiDAR the pipeline reads from Drive at 1 m (cutout)
or 5 m (region) – just thrown away. Across the border it's SRTM v3 or
Viewfinder Panoramas fill, so NOT LiDAR.
CAUTION, IT'S A COMPROMISE THE REPOSITORY ONCE REJECTED. It differs from
`sonny` (20m GeoTIFF) not in the horizontal grid but in the VERTICAL step:
model   format    horizontal     vertical
20m     GeoTIFF   20 × 20 m      0.1 m
1 m steps give a stepped slope that tears a continuous wall into a heap of
false fragments (figures in workers/README.md): the same rock area, but 2.5×
more broken pieces with a coarser outline. For ROCKS `sonny` (better still
`dmr5`) is the better choice; 1″ makes sense where the 20m model doesn't
reach, or for comparison.
`cell_m` is 31, not 20: the grid is asymmetric and estimates as well as
`rock_res: auto` should follow the WORSE axis (30.9 m along the meridian).
`rock-areas.py` measures the real cell from the raster anyway.
IT NEEDS A DRIVE SIGN-IN, and not for a quota: all 15 tiles are SHORTCUTS
to files elsewhere. A public `uc?export=download` of a shortcut answers
“Only the owner and editors can download this file” and `gdown --folder`
fails on it. `workers/drive/folder.py` resolves shortcuts through the Drive API.
.hgt → GeoTIFF is the standard path: 3601² is a size GDAL knows as SRTMHGT,
so `hgt_to_tif` in `update-dem.yml` needs no VRT workaround.

dmr35.label: ÚGKK DMR 3.5 (open data)
_comment: WORKS. Verified by run 31125042584: a 2319 MB ZIP holding one 42692×20429
raster, grid EXACTLY 10.0×10.0 m, CRS S-JTSK / Krovak East North. Cut into
15 tiles (1315 MB) and uploaded to the `dem-dmr35` release. The first ÚGKK
model the pipeline can take directly – and twice as fine as Sonny.
Another machine than DMR 5.0, and that was the point: `opendata.skgeodesy.sk`
is static storage, not ArcGIS behind a map client. `zbgis.` and `zbgisws.`
time out from a GitHub runner; this one answered on the first try.
With a 10 m grid it's TWICE as fine as Sonny (20 m) – and the source grid is
the only thing that caps real rock detail. `rock_res: auto` follows it: its
floor is a tenth of the DEM cell, so it drops from 2 m to 1 m.
`cell_m: 10` is measured after unpacking, not guessed from the file name
(`workers/dem/fetch-open.py` prints it into every run's summary).

dmr5.label: ÚGKK DMR 5.0 (LiDAR)
dmr5._comment_coverage: Mountain packages only (`mountain/outline.py`): a range ends where this OSM relation (Slovakia) does. Regions don't read it.
_comment: ONE SOURCE, TWO FORMS – and the EXTENT decides, not a second form choice:
with a cutout (`area`)   ugkk-<cutout>.tif in release dem-ugkk, full 1 m
whole region             tiles N49E019.tif in dem-dmr5-v2, resampled to 5 m
WHY `-v2` IN THE STORE NAME. Tiles are read from the 4 m pyramid into 5 m
cells – a 1.25 ratio, at which `-r average` skips source cells in a rhythm
that hillshade turns into a regular light-dark GRID. The fix is in
`workers/drive/dmr5-cut.py` (kernel from `workers/lib/cell.py`), the figures
in `workers/dem/measure-resampling.py`.
The file name `N49E020.tif` must NOT change – it's a promise about extent
(rule 2). So the store name carries the form, as `-v4` does for shading.
Without it `check-dem` would find the old tiles, decide “we have the model”
and the map would stay grainy with a green build.
It was two sources (`dmr5` and `ugkk`) but never two models – it's one LiDAR
that can't be stored twice. At 1 m a 1°×1° tile is ~48 GB and a release asset
caps at 2 GB, so a whole region at 1 m has nowhere to go.
WHERE IT COMES FROM: the `DMR 5.0 from Drive` workflow (dmr5-drive.yml). The
ETRS89 version of DMR 5.0 lies as two bare BigTIFFs on Google Drive, read
through HTTP Range:
dmr5_etrs89.tif      145.39 GiB  423 518 × 207 589 px, 1 m, LZW, 128² tiles
dmr5_etrs89.tif.ovr   43.35 GiB  pyramids 2 … 256 m
CRS EPSG:3046 (ETRS89 / TM zone N34), origin X 191 148, Y 5 497 220
Each tile is compressed on its own and Range works at any offset, so only
what the cutout crosses is read: the High Tatras (30.8 × 18.2 km) at 1 m take
10 min, 1.55 GB downloaded, a 1 203 MB COG – under the 2 GB asset cap.
HEIGHTS: ellipsoidal in the source (ETRS89), +42.6 m above Bpv. The workflow
converts them through EGM2008; Gerlach checks 2 697.03 → 2 653.92 m against
the official 2 654.4 m.
The keys below record the ZBGIS endpoints that were tried and time out from
a GitHub runner – not a path used today.
_comment_fallback: Paths are tried in order: direct URLs (when given) → service discovery from
the RPI metadata catalog (another host) → ArcGIS ImageServer → WCS. Each
request goes with browser headers (Safari, Chrome, then an ArcGIS client) and
finally through curl with HTTP/2 – WAFs block by TLS fingerprint too, not only
by User-Agent. The last resort is downloading DMR 5.0 once by hand into a release.
_comment_zip: THE PATH TO 1 m LIDAR THAT DOESN'T GO THROUGH ZBGIS. `opendata.skgeodesy.sk`
also holds the whole DMR 5.0 as one ZIP of ~198 GB – too big to download and
unpack (a runner has ~60 GB free, artifacts and assets cap at 2 GB), hence
of 151.43 GB with 46.28 GB of pyramids, a world file, metadata and a licence.
uses HTTP Range, and the 512×512 DEFLATE tiles are fetched only as needed. The
retired `DMR 5.0 from the ÚGKK archive` workflow (dmr5.yml) did this; it stays
here as a note on the source, not a path the pipeline uses.
MIND THE COST: a deflated ZIP entry can't be skipped into, so reading costs as
much as how far into the file the data lies – north is cheap, south expensive.
`verified: false` means the URL hasn't been read from a runner. `cell_m: 5` is
a choice, not a property: the source is 1 m, but all of Slovakia at 1 m won't

_comment: Mountain packages: one range in more detail than its regions carry – 2 m
contours, rocks and a height model from DMR 5.0 at 1 m, roads, paths, water,
points and aerial photos. Published under `mountains.ranges` in `maps.json`, a
category of its own, built by “Map · Build mountain package”. A range ends where
its height model does: its outline is cut to DMR 5.0's coverage (Slovakia), so
no part of it is drawn from Sonny's 20 m model.
country    key in `regions` whose data it is mostly made of
area       the cut-out in `areas` – its name, bbox and DMR 5.0 at 1 m
countries  ISO codes of every country it lies in
osm        osm.fr extracts below `/extracts/`, cut to the bbox and merged
outline    OSM relations (TANAP) whose areas inside the bbox are its edge;
`workers/mountain/outline.py --all` writes every range's edge, its
areas and box within DMR 5.0, to `outlines/<range>.geojson`
settings   what it is built with, over `maps.mountains.settings` and `defaults`
Data authors and licences, in the shape the app reads (`LayerCredit`).
A source names them in its `credits`; a package names the source kind in `sources` of
packages.json (`dem:contours`, `aerial:summer`) and gets the authors of the source its map used.
`copyright: false` = a source without ©.

author.work: Hillshading, 3D terrain, contours and rock faces

svet.name: World
svet.note: The base world map from its own pipeline (world-map.yml). `osmfr` is deliberately ABSENT: it's built not from a regional PBF but from OSM coastlines, Natural Earth and the Geofabrik index (workers/world/sources.py). `admin_level: 2` means the package sits on Drive directly in `svet/`, with no region level.

svet_basic.name: World – basic
svet_basic.note: The world map in its `basic` form – state borders and download regions only, no water or lakes (input `variant` in world-map.yml, lookup workers/data/world-variants.json). ITS OWN KEY, not a suffix to `svet`, by rule 2 of CLAUDE.md: a name is a promise about extent, so `basic` must not land on `svet.zip` or its node in `maps.json` – whoever downloads “the world map” from the catalog must not get a map without seas. So `country` is `svet_basic` too: the package sits in its own Drive folder and is its own root node in the catalog, beside `svet`.

svet_ground.name: World – ground
svet_ground.note: The world map in its `ground` form – sea, lakes, state borders and their names, no download regions (input `variant` in world-map.yml). Its own key for the reason `svet_basic` has one. The app bundles it as the ground of a map with nothing to draw.

navigacia_slovensko.name: Navigation – Slovakia
navigacia_slovensko.note: The routing GRAPH (Valhalla), not a map – `navigation.yml`, extent from workers/data/routing-areas.json. `osmfr` is deliberately ABSENT: `workers/routing/pbf.sh` downloads the PBF by that lookup, since the graph's extent is another question than the map's – the graph is NOT split by region (see there). `admin_level: 2` means the package sits on Drive directly in `navigacia_slovensko/`, with no region level. And `country` EQUALS the key – not a shared `navigacia` for every scope: `admin_level: 2` makes the country a catalog node too, so two scopes under one `navigacia` would OVERWRITE each other's item (both packages on Drive, the catalog knowing the second). The same decision for the same reason as `svet_basic`.

navigacia_slovensko_susedia.name: Navigation – Slovakia and neighbours
navigacia_slovensko_susedia.osm_name: Slovensko + CZ, AT, HU, PL, UA
navigacia_slovensko_susedia.note: The same as `navigacia_slovensko`, with a graph across borders – without it one can't drive to Austria, so neither avoid lacking a vignette there. ITS OWN KEY, not a suffix (rule 2): whoever downloads `navigacia_slovensko` from the catalog must not get a graph that ends at the border – nor the reverse. Its own `country` (and so its own catalog node) for the same reason as `navigacia_slovensko`.

slovensko.name: Slovakia
slovensko.note: All of Slovakia as one region – and the PARENT of its regions: each has `osmfr.parent: slovensko` and `workers/plan/pbf.sh` cuts it out of this extract (`osmium extract -s smart`). osm.fr's ready `{region}-latest.osm.pbf` is NOT USED – it isn't referentially complete, so an area reaching into a neighbouring region (CHKO Malé Karpaty, CHKO Záhorie, the Záhorie forests) lacks members and Planetiler drops it WHOLE, the in-region part too. Measured, with figures in the pbf.sh header. `iso` is the two-letter country code, here for ROUTING: an archive edge carries its country, or the vignette has nothing to stand on (`workers/data/vignettes.json`). Regions take it through their `country`, so it's written once. `routing_area` is the key in `workers/data/routing-areas.json` the CCH NODE ORDER is computed over – every region of a country must stand on the same one, or their archives must not be joined on the phone.

navigacia_cesko.name: Navigation – Czechia
navigacia_cesko.note: The routing graph of Česko alone – the same decision as `navigacia_slovensko`.

navigacia_rakusko.name: Navigation – Austria
navigacia_rakusko.note: The routing graph of Rakúsko alone – the same decision as `navigacia_slovensko`.

cesko.name: Czechia
cesko.note: Like `slovensko`: the whole country and the PARENT its regions are cut from. No elevation model covers it yet: `workers/data/map-settings.json` turns contours, rocks and hillshading off for it and its regions; the OSM layers are built as anywhere.

rakusko.name: Austria
rakusko.note: Like `slovensko`: the whole country and the PARENT its regions are cut from. No elevation model covers it yet: `workers/data/map-settings.json` turns contours, rocks and hillshading off for it and its regions; the OSM layers are built as anywhere.

_comment: Named cutouts for the `rock_area` input of the Build map workflow.
Rocks are the costliest part of a build (~30 min per region); when tuning
settings there's no point computing a whole region for one range.
The bbox is west,south,east,north in WGS84 and deliberately a bit larger than
the range itself – rather a little extra than a clipped ridge.
The workflow always intersects it with the chosen region's bbox too.
